title: Heated throw deals UK: today's best prices and which to buy
seoTitle: Heated Throw Deals UK: Best Prices and Which to Buy
description: Today's UK heated throw prices, from a £26.50 Slumberdown at Amazon to the Silentnight Super Cosy at £45.49, plus running costs and target prices.
intro:
**The best heated throw deal today is the Silentnight Luxury Super Cosy Heated Throw at £45.49 on Amazon, down from £59.99 and in line with the cheapest big retailers.** If you just want something warm for the sofa on a budget, the Slumberdown Luxury Heated Throw is £26.50 at Amazon, the same price it was earlier this month.

A heated throw costs about 2.5–4p an hour to run on full power, far less than heating the room. Prices below were checked on PriceSpy on 19 November 2026, the day [Amazon Black Friday Week](/guides/amazon-black-friday-2026-uk/) started.

body:
## Which heated throw should you buy?

Heated throws all do the same basic job, so the choice comes down to fabric, size, controls and brand. Here's the short version.

- **Cheapest that's still a known brand:** the **Slumberdown** throw at £26.50. Fine for occasional use on the sofa.
- **Best all-rounder:** the **Silentnight Luxury Super Cosy** at £45.49. It's the softest of the mainstream throws, with nine heat settings and a two-hour auto-off. Reviewers note you can see the heating wires through the knit, and one corner can run slightly cooler, but it's warm and well made.
- **With a remote:** the **Sensio Home** throw at £29.99 comes with a wireless remote, handy if you don't want the controller trailing across the sofa.
- **Plain and simple:** Silentnight's standard **Luxury Heated Throw** (£45 at Boots) or the **Carmen** fleece (£40 at Amazon).

If you're buying for a bed rather than the sofa, get an underblanket instead: they use less power and are designed for overnight use. Our [electric blanket deals guide](/guides/electric-blanket-deals-uk/) covers those.

## What a heated throw costs to run

Most heated throws draw 100–150W on their highest setting. At the current Ofgem price cap of 26.32p per kWh (1 October to 31 December 2026), that's about **2.5–4p an hour** on full heat, and less once it's warm and you turn it down. A two-hour evening on the sofa costs well under 10p.

Compare that with a 2kW fan heater at about 53p an hour. Warming yourself rather than the room is the cheapest way to stay comfortable on cold evenings. Our [cheapest heater to run guide](/guides/cheapest-heater-to-run-uk/) has the full comparison, and a [heated clothes airer](/guides/heated-clothes-airer-deals-uk/) is the other cheap winter buy worth a look.

## Features worth paying for

- **Auto-off.** A timer that switches the throw off after one to three hours is the most useful safety feature, especially if you doze off on the sofa.
- **Several heat settings.** Six to ten settings let you heat up fast and then turn it right down.
- **Detachable controller and machine washable.** Throws get grubby fast; check the label before buying.
- **Size.** 120 x 160cm covers one person. For two on a sofa, look for 160 x 180cm or bigger.
- **Overheat protection.** Most brand-name throws have it. Skip unbranded throws from marketplace sellers, which often lack it.

## Good prices to aim for

- **Budget fleece or flannel throw:** £25–£35
- **Silentnight Luxury Heated Throw:** about £45
- **Silentnight Super Cosy or other knit and sherpa throws:** £40–£50 is a good price; £60 is the full price
- **Faux-fur or extra-large throws:** £70–£80 is fair, though Argos lists Dreamland's faux-fur throws at £130

Heated throws are seasonal, so the best prices usually come in November, around Black Friday on 27 November, and again in January clearance sales. Popular colours sell out in cold snaps, so if you see a good price on the one you want, don't hang about. They also make a practical Christmas present; see our [Christmas gift guides](/christmas-gifts/) and [every Black Friday 2026 guide](/black-friday/) for more.

## Safety tips

- Buy a brand-name throw from a big retailer, not an unknown marketplace seller.
- Don't use a heated throw as overnight bedding, and don't sleep under it unless it has auto-off.
- Never use it folded or bunched up while it's on, and store it loosely rolled.
- Check the cable and controller each winter, and replace any throw with scorch marks or damage.
- Don't buy second-hand.

## FAQs

### Are heated throws cheap to run?

Yes. At today's price cap, most cost 2.5–4p an hour on full power, and less on lower settings. That's a fraction of the cost of running a fan or oil heater.

### Is it safe to fall asleep under a heated throw?

It's best not to. Heated throws are designed for the sofa, not overnight use. If you tend to doze off, choose one with an auto-off timer, such as the Silentnight Super Cosy, which switches off after two hours.

### Can you wash a heated throw?

Most can be machine washed on a gentle, cool cycle once you unplug the controller. Always check the care label, and make sure it's completely dry before using it again.

### Will heated throws be cheaper on Black Friday?

Some will drop a little further, but many are already discounted. The Silentnight Super Cosy is nearly a quarter off on Amazon until 30 November, and the Slumberdown has held at £26.50 all month, so there's little reason to wait if it's cold now.

### Heated throw or electric blanket: which is better?

Use a throw for the sofa and an electric underblanket for bed. Underblankets use less power and are made for overnight use; throws are bigger, softer and easier to move around the house.
